Turn on when the CLIP file is .gguf; keep it off for .safetensors (fp8). They must match — a mismatch fails with Value not in list (the native loader rejects .gguf, and the GGUF loader crashes on fp8).
Turn on to run the finished image through VOSR2 (2x) before saving; off saves the raw output. It is a lazy switch — when off the upscaler really does not run, so turning it off also saves the time.

When on, your prompt is first rewritten by the local model into a finished prompt, and that goes to the image model; when off, your prompt goes through untouched. It is a lazy switch — the enhancer really does not run when off, and a local rewrite takes tens of seconds, so turning it off saves that too.

Local gguf model used for rewriting. A bigger model follows instructions better but needs more VRAM: 4B ≈ 4.5 GB, 9B Q4_K_M ≈ 5.5 GB — both fit an 8 GB card, because the enhancer unloads itself before generation starts.
Large factors will run out of VRAM — keep it at or below 1 on 8 GB cards (0.5 is enough)
